index.summary: Core CLI forwarding and execution interception engine (dogdouclix.exe) on Windows with argument pass-through, full I/O stream streaming, WinStation/Desktop session inheritance, exit code fidelity, and context transformations.

product.objective: Build the core CLI forwarding and execution interception engine (dogdouclix.exe) on Windows, providing transparent argument pass-through, full I/O standard stream streaming, WinStation/Desktop session inheritance, exit code fidelity, and configurable context transformations (environment variable mutation and user context switching) for credential protection and profile sharing.

index.summary: Windows CLI forwarding executable (dogdouclix.exe) capable of spawning target binaries with verbatim arguments, inherited I/O streams, and exit code propagation.

deliverable.description: Core CLI forwarding binary and process execution engine.

index.summary: Context transformation engine supporting environment variable insertion, modification, and redaction, as well as execution under specified user security contexts.

deliverable.description: Context transformation subsystem for environment variable mutations and user context management.

index.summary: Automated test suite verifying argument escaping fidelity, standard stream pass-through, exit code return, environment modifications, and signal/cancellation handling.

deliverable.description: Test harness and automated integration tests.

included.item: CLI invocation forwarding: transparent wrapper dispatching target binary.
Command-line argument pass-through preserving verbatim quotes and escapes.
Standard stream (stdin, stdout, stderr) bidirectional streaming with binary and text fidelity.
WinStation and Desktop station inheritance (lpDesktop / Win32 process creation).
Target process exit code propagation and signal / Ctrl+C handling.
Context transformations: environment variable injection, override, and removal.

excluded.item: GUI process virtualization or window wrapping.
Network proxying or remote daemon execution.

requirement.statement: clix must transparently forward all command-line arguments to the target executable without altering argument escaping, whitespace, or quoting.
requirement.rationale: Callers expect identical CLI behavior as if invoking the target binary directly.

requirement.statement: clix must stream stdin, stdout, and stderr between caller and target process in real time with high fidelity and zero unwanted buffering.
requirement.rationale: Interactive CLI tools and piped pipelines rely on immediate stream transmission and preserved binary streams.

requirement.statement: clix must inherit or forward Windows station, desktop (lpDesktop), and console session properties to the child process.
requirement.rationale: Console applications require accurate console handles and window station contexts to function properly.

index.summary: Exit code fidelity and signal propagation.

requirement.statement: clix must return the exact exit code of the target child process and properly propagate termination signals (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Break).
requirement.rationale: Automation scripts, CI pipelines, and parent shells depend on accurate process exit codes and signal handling.

requirement.statement: clix must allow injecting, overriding, or redacting environment variables and executing under configured user security contexts before launching the child process.
requirement.rationale: Enables secret protection (temporary secret injection without polluting parent caller environment) and cross-user profile sharing.

acceptance.criterion: Target binary receives identical command-line arguments (including special characters, spaces, and quotes) as passed to clix.
Stdin, stdout, and stderr are streamed concurrently in real time, and pipeline redirection works transparently.
The exit code returned by clix matches the child process exit code across all termination cases (0, non-zero, crash).
Configured environment variables are successfully inserted, modified, or removed in the child process without leaking into caller process environment.
Process creation supports launching under alternate user security tokens/contexts where requested.
